# Patches carried on top of llama.cpp

<!-- GENERATED by `python3 .github/check-patches.py --render` from llama/patches/*.patch -- do not edit;
     the code-style job fails when this page is stale. -->

Every native library this project ships is built from the pinned llama.cpp source with the patches
below applied, in this order (`llama/cmake/apply-llama-patches.cmake`). They are the difference
between a java-llama.cpp binary and upstream's: bug fixes upstream has not merged yet, and the
embedding glue a JVM needs that upstream will not carry. Each is submitted upstream where it is
upstream-shaped, and dropped here the moment upstream carries the fix (the drop-checks are in
`CLAUDE.md`, "Local llama.cpp source patches"). Every natives jar names the ids it was built with
in its `jllama-build.txt` (`patches=`) and a hash over the set (`patches.sha256=`), so a consumer can
match a binary to this page.

**13 patches.** Ids as `jllama-build.txt` lists them under `patches=`.

## 0001-win32-arg-parse-embed-guard.patch

**Files (35):** `common/arg.cpp`, `common/arg.h`, `examples/batched/batched.cpp`, `examples/debug/debug.cpp`, `examples/diffusion/diffusion-cli.cpp`, `examples/embedding/embedding.cpp`, `examples/eval-callback/eval-callback.cpp`, `examples/idle/idle.cpp`, `examples/lookahead/lookahead.cpp`, `examples/lookup/lookup-create.cpp`, `examples/lookup/lookup-stats.cpp`, `examples/lookup/lookup.cpp`, `examples/parallel/parallel.cpp`, `examples/passkey/passkey.cpp`, `examples/retrieval/retrieval.cpp`, `examples/speculative-simple/speculative-simple.cpp`, `examples/speculative/speculative.cpp`, `examples/training/finetune.cpp`, `tests/test-arg-parser.cpp`, `tests/test-export-graph-ops.cpp`, `tests/test-thread-safety.cpp`, `tools/batched-bench/batched-bench.cpp`, `tools/cli/cli.cpp`, `tools/completion/completion.cpp`, `tools/cvector-generator/cvector-generator.cpp`, `tools/export-lora/export-lora.cpp`, `tools/fit-params/fit-params.cpp`, `tools/imatrix/imatrix.cpp`, `tools/mtmd/debug/mtmd-debug.cpp`, `tools/mtmd/mtmd-cli.cpp`, `tools/perplexity/perplexity.cpp`, `tools/results/results.cpp`, `tools/server/server.cpp`, `tools/tokenize/tokenize.cpp`, `tools/tts/tts.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
common: parse exactly the argv an embedding caller passes (no GetCommandLineW override)

Since llama.cpp #24779 (b9739) common_params_parse re-derives argv from the PROCESS command line on
Windows and adopts it, so an embedded caller -- java.exe hosting libjllama through JNI -- loses the
`--model ...` it passed and the load fails with "Failed to parse model parameters". b9789 narrowed
that to a count guard, which still fires whenever the embedded argv happens to have the length of
java.exe's own. This patch keeps common_params_parse to the argv it is given and moves the UTF-8
recovery for the standalone tools into a new common_params_parse_main(), which every tool's main()
now calls; a regression case in tests/test-arg-parser.cpp pins the contract. The embedded caller
(jllama.cpp) keeps calling common_params_parse. Reported upstream as ggml-org/llama.cpp#26416;
carried here until upstream decides which of the two directions it wants.

Touches common/arg.{cpp,h} and the ~34 standalone main() call sites, which this project does not
compile (LLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS/TESTS are OFF for a FetchContent subproject) but keeps in the patch so it
can be submitted verbatim.
```

## 0002-server-preserve-caller-load-progress-callback.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server-context.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: keep a load-progress callback the embedding caller installed

Since b9789 server_context::load_model unconditionally installs the server's own load-progress
reporter on params_base.load_progress_callback right before common_init_from_params, clobbering the
callback an embedding caller set -- libjllama wires LoadProgressCallback to a JNI trampoline before
load_model, so Java saw no progress and the abort-on-false path never fired. The guard installs the
server's reporter only when no callback is set OR when the one set is the server's own: load_model
runs a second time on wake from the sleeping state (--sleep-idle-seconds), and a bare nullptr check
would then leave user_data pointing at the dead stack frame of the first call (segfault on the
first request after an idle window). Standalone llama-server is unaffected.
```

## 0003-pr22393-server-add-slot-prompt-similarity-getter-setter.patch

**Files (2):** `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, `tools/server/server-context.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
Upstream PR: ggml-org/llama.cpp#22393 — "server : add slot_prompt_similarity getter/setter"
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22393

Carried locally until the PR is merged upstream. Adds public get/set accessors for the
server_context `slot_prompt_similarity` field so an embedding/JNI caller can query and tune
the slot-selection threshold at runtime without reloading the model. The change is purely
additive (two new accessors + their declarations) and is a verbatim copy of the upstream PR,
so it can be dropped from patches/ once b<nnnn> includes it. Refresh against the new source on
every llama.cpp version bump (the applier fails loud if the context shifts).

Update: upstream closed PR #22393 without merging -- ngxson rejected it, reasoning that
slot_prompt_similarity is internal, single-use-case state that shouldn't be exposed as public
API and should instead live in downstream code. This patch is therefore now carried
indefinitely, not pending-merge; it will never be droppable via an upstream bump and must keep
being refreshed on every version bump.
```

## 0006-server-embed-native-server-jni.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: make llama_server() embeddable in a host process (no signal handlers, forwarded argv, stoppable)

b9870 exposes int llama_server(int, char **) with no main() in server.cpp; this patch adds what a
JVM host needs to run it inside libjllama: a g_llama_server_embedded flag with
llama_server_set_embedded() / llama_server_request_shutdown() (declared by the host in
native_server_bridge.h), no process-wide SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers in embedded mode (they would
hijack the JVM's), common_params_parse instead of common_params_parse_main for the forwarded argv
(the latter's GetCommandLineW recovery would pick up java.exe's command line, the class of defect
0001 fixes), and a shutdown handler guarded by g_shutdown_handler_mutex and reset before the locals
it captures are destroyed -- a request landing after llama_server() returned used to run the lambda
over destroyed objects (SIGSEGV in server_http_context::stop(), seen in router mode).
Runnable guard: src/test/cpp/test_native_server_shutdown.cpp. Applies after 0001.
```

## 0007-server-attach-http-frontend.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: let an embedding host attach the HTTP frontend to an already-loaded server_context

Adds llama_server_attach(argc, argv, server_context &, server_routes &), which serves a model the
host has already loaded over the upstream HTTP frontend: no second model load, no start_loop() --
the host's worker keeps driving the shared server_context and the HTTP routes post tasks to its
queue. The stable route table is factored out of llama_server() into
llama_server_register_common_routes(), byte-identical to the block it replaces (the invariant to
re-check on every bump); the attach entry point registers it plus the non-router resumable-streaming
handlers and the GCP shim, answers /cors-proxy and /tools with 403 (the MCP/tools host belongs to a
full llama-server), marks ready immediately and blocks in ctx_http.join() until
llama_server_request_shutdown(). It serves the caller's server_routes rather than a frame-local one:
server_routes' constructor registers a sleeping-state callback on the model's task queue that
outlives the attach call. Applies after 0001 and 0006.
```

## 0008-server-models-worker-cmd-override.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server-models.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: let the router spawn its model workers through a host-supplied command (LLAMA_SERVER_WORKER_CMD)

The router (server-models.cpp) starts each model worker by re-executing its own binary
(get_server_exec_path(): /proc/self/exe and friends). Inside a JVM that binary is java, not a
llama-server, so embedded router workers could never start. The environment variable
LLAMA_SERVER_WORKER_CMD (whitespace-split, read in server_model_meta::update_args) replaces the
leading binary-path token of the rendered worker command, so a host relaunches workers through its
own bootstrap -- here `java -cp app.jar net.ladenthin.llama.server.NativeServer`, set from Java by
NativeServer.setWorkerCommand(). Also useful for containerised or wrapped deployments.
```

## 0014-common-log-callback-sink.patch

**Files (2):** `common/log.cpp`, `common/log.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
common: add a callback sink to common_log (common_log_set_callback)

An embedding host (here: the java-llama.cpp JNI binding) has no way to receive the
lines that common_log prints: llama_log_set() covers only llama/ggml, while the
server's SRV_*/SLT_* macros write straight into common_log and end up on stderr no
matter what the host configured. common_log offers file, colors, prefix, timestamps,
verbosity and JSONL, but no hook.

This adds common_log_set_callback(log, cb, user_data): while set, the worker thread
hands every entry to the callback instead of printing it (a file set via
common_log_set_file still receives it). The callback gets the formatted message
without prefix/timestamp/colors and has the ggml_log_callback signature, so one
function can serve both llama_log_set() and this sink. Swapping the callback pauses
the worker first, so entries already queued reach the previous sink.

Upstream-submittable ("common : add a callback sink to common_log for embedding
hosts"); not yet filed. Guarded by src/test/cpp/test_common_log_callback.cpp.
```

## 0015-rpc-embeddable-client-and-stoppable-server.patch

**Files (5):** `common/arg.cpp`, `ggml/include/ggml-rpc.h`, `ggml/src/ggml-rpc/ggml-rpc.cpp`, `ggml/src/ggml-rpc/transport.cpp`, `ggml/src/ggml-rpc/transport.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-rpc: let an embedding host register servers and stop its own server safely

An embedding host (here: the java-llama.cpp JNI binding, which runs llama.cpp inside a
JVM) cannot use ggml-rpc as it is:

1. Every client-side connection problem is a GGML_ABORT: a malformed endpoint, a server
   that is not running, a failed handshake. For a standalone tool that is an error exit;
   inside a JVM it kills the whole application because of a typo in "--rpc". The
   registration path now reports these as failures instead:
   - rpc_dispatcher::start() returns false;
   - try_get_dispatcher() returns nullptr;
   - ggml_backend_rpc_get_device_count() returns 0;
   - ggml_backend_rpc_add_server() returns nullptr.
   add_rpc_devices() (common/arg.cpp) now throws std::invalid_argument naming the server,
   where it used to register nullptr and silently run without the requested server.

   Every path that runs AFTER registration (buffer/graph/tensor calls) keeps the original
   contract through get_dispatcher(), which still aborts. A server that vanishes mid-run
   stays fatal; that needs a real error path through the backend interface.

2. add_server() returned a cached registration without checking that the server is still
   there, so re-using an endpoint whose server had stopped passed registration and aborted
   on the first tensor upload. The cache hit is now re-checked.

   ggml_backend_rpc_get_device_memory() of a server that went away reports 0/0 instead of
   aborting. Registered devices stay in ggml's process-wide registry forever, and code that
   never uses them still queries their memory: common_init() lists every device at -lv 4,
   and --list-devices does too. 0/0 is what --fit already reads as an unknown budget.
   ggml_backend_rpc_init() keeps aborting if the registration fails.

3. ggml_backend_rpc_start_server() cannot be stopped: while(true) around accept(). Two new
   entry points, both also exposed through get_proc_address:
   - ggml_backend_rpc_stop_server() disconnects the client being served and wakes accept()
     with a loopback connection (the one portable way to interrupt it). The loop then
     releases its backends; it used to never reach that code.
   - ggml_backend_rpc_server_listening() tells the host whether the socket was bound.
   The transport stays initialised on the way out, because WSACleanup() would invalidate
   every other RPC socket in the process.

4. transport: no SIGPIPE when the peer went away (MSG_NOSIGNAL / SO_NOSIGPIPE), a
   socket_t::shutdown(), and the file descriptors that connect()/create_server()/accept()
   leaked on their error paths are closed.

Upstream-submittable; not filed upstream yet. The runnable guard is
src/test/cpp/test_rpc.cpp: it links both new functions and exercises the registration and
stop paths over loopback.
```

## 0016-model-kolibri1.patch

**Files (6):** `src/llama-arch.cpp`, `src/llama-arch.h`, `src/llama-model.cpp`, `src/llama-vocab.cpp`, `src/models/kolibri1.cpp`, `src/models/models.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
model: add Kolibri-1 (kolibri1) -- carried until upstream supports it

Aleph Alpha's Kolibri-1 is a 78B-parameter German/English reasoning MoE (3.46B active per
token, Apache-2.0). Upstream llama.cpp has no support yet; the request is
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29922 (open, no PR at the time of writing).
DROP THIS PATCH as soon as upstream registers the architecture -- check on every bump with
`git grep -n kolibri src/llama-arch.cpp` in the new llama.cpp tag. This one is a clean true/false,
unlike the drop-checks of 0017, 0018 and 0019: the name reaches that file only through this patch,
so NO hits means the patch is still needed and any hit means upstream has it. Run it against the
pristine tag, never against a patched source tree, which would show this patch's own lines.
Measured at b11639 (a0e6dc738): 0 hits.

Architecture (from Aleph Alpha's own vLLM implementation, the reference used here):
  - GQA attention with per-head q/k RMSNorm. config.layer_types interleaves sliding-window
    layers, which use (NEOX) RoPE, with full-attention layers that have no positional encoding.
  - Sandwich norms: input norm -> attention -> post-attention norm -> residual, then
    pre-FFN norm -> routed MoE + one ungated shared expert -> post-FFN norm -> residual.
  - Router: top-k selected on (logits + expert_bias), experts weighted by the unbiased
    sigmoid(logits), renormalized only if norm_topk_prob (off in Kolibri-1). This is NOT
    DeepSeek-V3's sigmoid router (selection on sigmoid(logits) + bias), which picks other
    experts as soon as the bias is non-zero -- so the graph builds the selection itself and
    hands it to build_moe_ffn (selected_experts_in); build_moe_ffn itself is unchanged.

What the patch touches: the arch name "kolibri1" (llama-arch.{h,cpp}), the model mapping and
NEOX rope type (llama-model.cpp), the model struct (models/models.h), the new
src/models/kolibri1.cpp, and the "kolibri1" pre-tokenizer name mapped to Qwen2's
(llama-vocab.cpp). No converter or gguf-py change: this project only loads GGUFs.

Both published GGUF dialects load. The two community converters disagree on metadata, and
each community runtime rejects the other's files:
  - expert_gating_func: 2 (sigmoid) from the AFMoE-based converter, 5 ("sigmoid_logit_add",
    a value only the Qwen3-MoE-based converter's patch defines) from the other one, or
    absent. All three mean the same router, which is a property of the architecture.
  - tokenizer.ggml.pre: "qwen2" or "kolibri1"; the Qwen3-MoE-based runtime registers the
    latter, the AFMoE-based one does not (llama.cpp rejects an unknown pre-tokenizer).
  - expert_weights_norm, expert_shared_count and output.weight are optional here.

Known places (all read while writing this patch, 2026-10-06):
  - Request:   https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29922
  - Model:     https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 (and Kolibri-1-BF16)
  - Reference: https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/aleph-alpha-inference, aleph_alpha_inference/
               kolibri1.py at 049a6a7 (Apache-2.0, Copyright 2026 Aleph Alpha GmbH) -- the
               specification this patch follows; its tests/test_kolibri1.py pins the router.
  - AFMoE-based port by Eliasfpv28, base llama.cpp edd6e2bbd (b11378):
               https://huggingface.co/Eliasfpv28/Kolibri-1-Q3_K_S-GGUF, runtime-source/
               kolibri1-runtime.patch (new additions Apache-2.0, llama.cpp-derived parts MIT).
               Source of the graph-side router (selection built outside build_moe_ffn).
               Its runtime is also what https://huggingface.co/InsidiousFiddler/Kolibri-1-GGUF
               points to.
  - Qwen3-MoE-based port, base llama.cpp 836d571 (b11381), as carried in
               https://github.com/mjwsolo/localcode/pull/101 (patches/0006-kolibri1.patch,
               "community patch"). https://huggingface.co/Hob-forge/Kolibri-1-GGUF publishes
               GGUFs and a kolibri1-llama.cpp.patch (MIT) for the same base commit whose model
               card describes the same design (a new gating mode); that file itself could not be
               fetched from here, so it is not verified to be byte-identical. Source of the
               loader (optional keys, tied-output fallback, swa rope base) and of the graph layout.
  - Independent effort under the name "kolibri" (not "kolibri1"), whose GGUFs this patch
               does not load: https://github.com/CWBudde/kolibri-llama-cpp,
               https://github.com/CWBudde/llama.cpp/pull/7

Verification in java-llama.cpp: src/test/cpp/test_kolibri1.cpp builds tiny random Kolibri-1
GGUFs in both dialects, runs them through the real library and compares every logit with an
independent float reference written from the vLLM implementation above.
```

## 0017-ggml-cpu-x86-prefetch-byte-offset-and-msvc-type.patch

**Files (2):** `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/prefetch.h`, `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu(x86): byte-wise prefetch address, and a type clang accepts on MSVC targets

The four _mm_prefetch calls in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c (the SSSE3-without-AVX
branch of ggml_vec_dot_q4_0_q8_0) carry two independent defects. Both are fixed by routing the
address through one new static inline helper, ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/prefetch.h; the call
sites change from a raw expression to ggml_prefetch_at(&x[ib], sizeof(block_q4_0)) and nothing
else moves. The helper is header-only and included relatively, so no CMake change is needed.

1. Type -- this breaks the build on a current clang. MSVC declares the intrinsic as
   `void _mm_prefetch(char const *, int)`. Clang's own xmmintrin.h defines a macro that casts to
   `const void *`, but it sits behind `#ifndef _MSC_VER`: on a *-windows-msvc target clang leaves
   the declaration to Microsoft. Passing `const block_q4_0 *` is then
   -Wincompatible-pointer-types, which clang 22 promoted to an error by default (llvm-project
   #157364; the 22.1.0 release notes say "The -Wincompatible-pointer-types diagnostic now
   defaults to an error; it can still be downgraded to a warning by passing
   -Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types"). NOT clang 16 -- an earlier version of this header
   claimed that, but clang 16 promoted only -Wincompatible-FUNCTION-pointer-types.

   Measured on the real file at -msse4.2, plain clang (the GNU driver, which
   cmake/x64-windows-llvm.cmake selects) on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, before and after this patch:

     clang 20.1.8   unpatched -> 4 warnings, object file produced   patched -> 0 errors, 0 warnings
     clang 22.1.3   unpatched -> 4 errors,   no object file         patched -> 0 errors, 0 warnings
     clang 23.1.3   unpatched -> 4 errors,   no object file         patched -> 0 errors, 0 warnings

   (20.1.8 and 23.1.3 locally with MSVC 14.44.35207 headers; 20.1.8 and 22.1.3 on a
   windows-2025-vs2026 runner, which carries both.) The practical consequence is that
   -DGGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON cannot be built
   with a current plain clang on Windows, because the `sse42` variant compiles this branch: ggml
   passes it -msse4.2 (its `/arch:` branch is behind `if (MSVC)`, false for plain clang), which
   defines __SSSE3__ without __AVX__ and so selects `#elif defined(__SSSE3__)`. It is the only
   such variant -- the x86-64 baseline (`x64`) has no SSSE3 and takes the scalar branch, and
   every richer variant has AVX. -msse4.2 -mavx builds for that reason. clang-cl and MSVC are
   unaffected (the macro and the warning level differ), as is clang on a GNU target.

2. Arithmetic -- wrong on every platform, including where the call compiles.
   `&x[ib] + sizeof(block_q4_0)` adds sizeof() *elements*, not bytes. With the sizes that
   ggml-common.h pins by static_assert (block_q4_0 == 18, block_q8_0 == 34) the prefetch targets
   +324 and +1156 bytes instead of +18 and +34, and the "+ 2 *" pair targets +648 instead of
   +36 -- 18 and 34 times too far. The call sites plainly intend "the next block" and "two blocks
   ahead", which is what byte-wise arithmetic gives. Measured: no throughput difference on a
   Ryzen 7 5800H forced onto the sse42 kernel with a 0.6B Q4_0 model (pp512 101.3 vs 100.9,
   tg128 37.3 vs 37.0, both inside the other's error bars), so this is a correctness fix, not a
   performance one; a genuine SSE4.2-era machine was not available to measure.

Upstream-submittable, and intended to be submitted: the fix is confined to one new header plus
four call sites and changes no behaviour beyond the prefetch address.

Why upstream's own build is green -- measured, and no longer an open question. Their windows-cpu
release job builds exactly this with plain clang, GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON and no suppressing
flag (CMAKE_ARGS carries only build-target toggles), and ships ggml-cpu-sse42.dll. The reason it
works is the clang version: the windows-2025-vs2026 image has LLVM 20.1.8 on PATH, where these
are warnings. Note how narrow that is -- the same image also ships clang 22.1.3 inside Visual
Studio 2026 (VC/Tools/Llvm/x64), which fails on the unpatched file; upstream reaches the working
one only because C:\Program Files/LLVM/bin comes first on PATH. It was NOT a header difference
-- all three MSVC toolsets on that image
(14.29.30133, 14.44.35207, 14.51.36231) declare _mm_prefetch identically as
`extern void _mm_prefetch(char const*_A, int _Sel);`, which was the first hypothesis and is
disproved. So this patch is ahead of upstream rather than diverging from it: their build breaks
the moment the runner image ships a clang that makes the diagnostic fatal, and until then they
compile four warnings and a prefetch address that is 18x/34x too far.

Runnable guard: src/test/cpp/test_prefetch.cpp drives ggml_prefetch_at against the real
block_q4_0 / block_q8_0 types and asserts the offsets are byte-wise. That test is red if this
patch is dropped, and -- the case that matters -- also red if the cast is written around the
whole expression, `(const char *)(&x[ib] + sizeof(block_q4_0))`, which fixes (1) and silently
keeps (2).

On a bump, check whether upstream fixed this themselves:
`git grep -n _mm_prefetch ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c` in the new tag. That grep is a
LOCATOR, NOT A VERDICT -- it returns FOUR hits at every tag, because the calls exist either way
(measured at b11639 (a0e6dc738): lines 846, 847, 864, 865). Read them: the fix is upstream's only
when the cast to a byte pointer happens BEFORE the addition. `(const char *)(&x[ib] + sizeof(...))`
casts the whole expression, silences the compiler and keeps the wrong address, so it looks fixed and
is not -- test_prefetch.cpp is what tells those two apart. Only then DROP this patch rather than
refreshing it.
```

## 0018-ggml-amx-free-the-aligned-buffer.patch

**Files (1):** `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/amx/amx.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu(amx): free the AMX weight buffer with ggml_aligned_free(), not free()

ggml_backend_amx_buffer_type_alloc_buffer() allocates the buffer that holds the AMX-repacked
weights with ggml_aligned_malloc(), and ggml_backend_amx_buffer_free_buffer() releases it with
free(). On Linux that pair is fine (posix_memalign memory is free()-able). On Windows
ggml_aligned_malloc() is _aligned_malloc(), whose memory only _aligned_free() may release: free()
on it corrupts the CRT heap, and the process dies with STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xC0000374) the
moment the model is unloaded -- after inference worked. The CPU buffer type next to it already
does it right (ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_free_buffer -> ggml_aligned_free), and ggml_aligned_free()
is free() on Linux, so nothing changes there.

Reached by: a Windows build whose chosen CPU module carries AMX (GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS ->
ggml-cpu-sapphirerapids, which ggml_backend_load_best() picks on Sapphire, Emerald and Granite
Rapids; ggml_amx_init() returns true unconditionally on _WIN32) and a model with weight types that
have AMX kernels (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ4_XS). Found by java-llama.cpp's Publish
run 38069595101 (2026-10-10): the Windows x86-64 Java test job landed on an "Intel(R) Xeon(R)
6973P-C" runner (Granite Rapids), loaded ggml-cpu-sapphirerapids.dll, ran two generations on
Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, and the fork died with exit code -1073740940 (0xC0000374) at the
model's close(); the same job was green an hour earlier (run 38065017595) on an AMD EPYC 7763
runner, which has no AVX-512 and loads the haswell module. Upstream master still had the free()
on 2026-10-10. Not yet reported upstream (nothing is filed before this project's release).

Every other caller of ggml_aligned_malloc() in the tree pairs it correctly -- ggml-backend.cpp,
ggml-cpu.c (twice), ggml-openvino.cpp, ggml-zdnn.cpp and ggml.c itself -- so this was the one
mismatched pair, and ggml-backend.cpp:2464 is the line this fix copies.

Reproduced deliberately afterwards, rather than waiting for CI to draw AMX hardware again: on a
rented Granite Rapids machine, one CPU backend module staged at a time, same model, same binaries:

    module            runs  exit
    sapphirerapids       6   -1073740940 (0xC0000374)   <- the only module with the AMX path
    cooperlake           2   0
    icelake              2   0
    haswell              2   0

The same six runs on Linux with the same CPU all exit 0 with byte-identical output. It reproduces at
one thread, so it is not a data race, and the crash lands after the inference has printed its
timings -- the signature of a heap corrupted earlier and detected at free. With this patch applied,
the identical matrix on the same machine gives exit 0 in all twelve runs.

Guard on the downstream side: llama/cmake/check-aligned-free-pairing.cmake fails the configure on
any platform when a ggml source calls ggml_aligned_malloc() and never ggml_aligned_free(). A
run-time test cannot replace it -- without an AMX CPU there is nothing to observe, which is exactly
how this shipped.

Drop this patch when upstream frees the AMX buffer with ggml_aligned_free() or _aligned_free():
grep "free(buffer->context)" ggml/src/ggml-cpu/amx/amx.cpp at the new tag. NOTE THE INVERSION --
a hit means the bare free() is STILL THERE and this patch is still needed; it is droppable when the
grep prints NOTHING. Measured at b11639 (a0e6dc738): one hit, line 46, so the defect stands.
```

## 0019-ggml-cpu-select-the-neon-fp32-to-fp16-conversion.patch

**Files (1):** `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/simd-mappings.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu : select the NEON fp32->fp16 conversion

The __ARM_NEON branch of ggml/src/ggml-cpu/simd-mappings.h defines both
GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_FP16_TO_FP32 and GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_FP32_TO_FP16 but selects only the first, so
GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16 falls through to GGML_COMPUTE_FP32_TO_FP16 at the end of that section --
ggml-base's deliberately portable software bit manipulation, the one ggml.c uses everywhere
because ggml-base may not assume CPU features -- while neon_compute_fp32_to_fp16, a one-line
__fp16 conversion, stays defined and referenced by nothing. The whole purpose of the GGML_CPU_*
pair is to be the accelerated variant; on ARM it was defined to be the unaccelerated one.

__POWER9_VECTOR__ and __riscv_zfhmin select both macros, and the comment on that fallback has
always said NEON does too ("so we define GGML_CPU_FP16_TO_FP32 and GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16
elsewhere for NEON. This is also true for POWER9."). Not a regression: the NEON selection is
absent in all 25 most recent commits touching the file, back to 2025-04-10.

Why it is felt on ARM and nowhere else: ggml_cpu_fp32_to_fp16 -- the from_float of GGML_TYPE_F16
-- has vector paths for F16C, RISC-V and s390x (the last added in llama.cpp #30157) and none for
NEON, so there the whole function is the scalar loop through the macro.

THE GUARD, AND WHY ITS FIRST HALF HAS A CARVE-OUT. In place of the stale fallback comment an
#error pair refuses a branch that defines a COMPUTE macro without selecting it -- the omission
that neither a build, a warning nor a test could see, because the fallback silently supplies a
correct implementation, so the only symptom is a hardware instruction nothing ever reaches. The
FP16->FP32 half carries `&& !defined(__F16C__)`, with the issue link on the condition line,
because llama.cpp #30343 (upstream commit 685f70894) puts that one direction back on the lookup
table on purpose: clang lowers the F16C intrinsic into the live accumulator register of the
quantized dot products and serialises the loop, 45-65 % slower Q8_0/Q4_0 MUL_MAT_ID kernels.
Without the carve-out the guard would fire on every x86 build with F16C -- here that is 11 of the
14 x86-64 CPU variant modules. The FP32->FP16 half needs no exception: F16C, NEON (with this
patch), POWER9 and riscv_zfhmin all select it. Should #30342 ever be resolved and the F16C
selection come back, the carve-out becomes dead weight and should be deleted; that is what the
link on that line is for.

The guard's position -- immediately before the fallback rather than directly after the #elif
chain -- was chosen by a mutation measurement, not by taste: before the fallback it catches 4 of
4 correctness cases with no false alarms, while directly after the chain it misses one (a COMPUTE
macro defined after the chain and never selected) and, since #30343, fails every x86 F16C build
outright, because that commit leaves the F16C selection below the lookup-table declarations.

THIS DIFF APPLIES BOTH AT THE PIN AND ON UPSTREAM MASTER, because it no longer touches the F16C
block at all. An earlier version of this patch also moved #30270's two F16C selections into the
__F16C__ branch; that was dropped when #30343 turned the block into a documented exception
carrying an issue link. At the pinned tag #30343 is not in yet, so the F16C block there still
selects both directions and the carve-out is inert -- x86 behaviour at the pin is exactly
upstream's. Once the pin crosses 685f70894 the carve-out becomes load-bearing.

WHY THIS PROJECT CARRIES IT. All 17 ARM artifacts shipped here -- cpu-linux-aarch64 (8 variants),
cpu-android-aarch64 (7), cpu-windows-aarch64 and metal-macos-aarch64 -- contain no fcvt of any
form in ggml_cpu_fp32_to_fp16, and neither do upstream's own llama-b11576-bin-ubuntu-arm64 and
-macos-arm64. A plain gcc with no flags defines __ARM_NEON and __ARM_FP16_FORMAT_IEEE on aarch64,
so there is no opt-in and no way to miss it.

MEASURED. The function runs 2.45x to 13.3x faster with the selection, across five ARM core types
(Ampere eMAG, Cortex-A55, Neoverse-N1, Neoverse-V2, Apple M1), three operating systems and nine
compiler builds, with the opposite direction measured in the same binary and run as a control that
stays within 3.2 % everywhere. Bit-exact: both paths agree on every one of the 2^32 float32 bit
patterns, differing only in NaN payload -- where the same comparison on x86 F16C gives the same
numbers, so this brings ARM into agreement with what x86 already ships. It is NOT an inference
speed-up: perf puts 83.9 % of an F16 pp512 run in tinyBLAS's gemm, which converts inside its own
microkernel, and 0.03 % in this function. The full record, including the mutation measurement that
chose the guard's position, is docs/benchmarks/arm-fp16-conversion.md.

Built in upstream's own ARM release configuration (GGML_BACKEND_DL, GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS,
GGML_NATIVE=OFF): all eight variant modules compile, the guard fires nowhere, fcvt/fcvtn/fcvtn2
appear in every one of them, reverting in the same tree puts that back to zero, and ctest gives
52 of 54 with the two failures identical on unpatched master. Verified again with clang -E against
the pinned source after the rebase: the guard is silent in all five configurations (x86 +F16C+AVX2,
+F16C+AVX512, sse42, plain x86, NEON), and fires when the NEON selection is removed again.

SUBMITTED UPSTREAM as ggml-org/llama.cpp#30505 (open), rebased onto master and byte-identical to
this diff.

On a bump, check whether upstream merged it. THE OUTPUT MUST BE READ, NOT TESTED -- run it against
the branch, so that "nothing" is the answer while the patch is needed:

  git show <pin>:ggml/src/ggml-cpu/simd-mappings.h \
    | sed -n '/^#if defined(__ARM_NEON)/,/^#elif/p' | grep -n GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16

One line printed means upstream merged it; then DROP this patch rather than refreshing it -- the
fail-loud applier detects "does not apply", never "upstream already fixed this".

Do NOT reduce the looser form
`git grep -n "GGML_CPU_FP32_TO_FP16(x) GGML_CPU_COMPUTE_FP32_TO_FP16" ggml/src/ggml-cpu/simd-mappings.h`
to a true/false: it returns THREE hits at every tag so far -- __POWER9_VECTOR__, __riscv_zfhmin and
the out-of-chain __F16C__ block -- and the first two carry the NEON line's four-space indentation, so
a `grep -q` reports "upstream fixed it" at every tag and deletes a fix that is still needed.
Measured at b11639 (a0e6dc738): hits at lines 71, 114 and 150, none of them inside the __ARM_NEON
branch, while `git apply --check` of this patch is clean -- the two answers contradict each other,
and the grep is the one that is wrong.
```

## 0020-ggml-alloc-validate-leafs-before-reusing-an-allocation.patch

**Files (1):** `ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-alloc : validate the leafs before reusing a graph's allocation

ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph() assigns every tensor of a graph by position from the previous
ggml_gallocr_reserve(): node i takes node_allocs[i], leaf i takes leaf_allocs[i].
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc() decides whether those assignments still fit, and it validates every
node and every node's sources -- but of the leafs it compares only the count. A graph with the
same number of leafs in another order therefore reuses the old leaf assignments: an input leaf
lands on a slot that belonged to a weight (buffer_id -1, nothing allocated), and with NDEBUG the
asserts in ggml_gallocr_init_tensor() are gone, so ggml_vbuffer_tensor_alloc() indexes
galloc->buffers[-1]. A leaf that lands on a slot of another input is not caught either: its size
is never checked, so it may get a region too small for it.

Reached since #30445 ("graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings", cb55ffe6e, b11574..b11612):
the models no longer expand their LM head themselves, build_logits() does, after build_pooling().
In a context with embeddings enabled the reserved graph expands t_embd first and t_logits
second; a generation step on the same context (the server switches embeddings off for a slot
that samples, llama_set_embeddings(ctx, false)) expands only t_logits, whose first source is
output.weight. Same node and leaf counts, every leaf after output.weight shifted by one. Found
by java-llama.cpp's Publish run 38648257387 (2026-10-14): ErrorHandlingTest loads its model with
--embedding and posts an infill request to it, and the forked JVM died with SIGSEGV in
ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph on Linux, and with 0xC0000005 under both Windows toolchains:

    ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph <- ggml_backend_sched_alloc_graph <- llama_context::process_ubatch
    <- llama_context::decode <- server_context_impl::update_slots

Reproduced locally with a random 2-layer llama GGUF (FIM tokens set) and a context of 128:
infill on the model without --embedding works, with --embedding it crashes; a debug print shows
leaf 31 'out_ids' arriving at a slot with no allocation. Reverting cb55ffe6e makes it pass, and
so does this patch, which validates the leafs exactly as the nodes are validated: an invalid
leaf makes the allocator reserve again (one buffer) or report false, on which
ggml_backend_sched reserves the graph itself. With it, greedy infill on the --embedding model
returns the same tokens as on the model without, run after run.

The guard is src/test/cpp/test_gallocr_leafs.cpp: two graphs with the same nodes in the same order
and only the leafs moved (it dies with SIGSEGV without this patch), reserve with one, allocate the other.

Drop-check on every bump: read ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc() in ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c at the new
tag -- once it walks graph->leafs itself, drop this patch rather than refreshing it.
```
